description:
=== DONE (s473t5d) ===
FOUND + FIXED s473t5d (Opus, 2026-09-13) by #1501 round 5, one layer down from
#1700: with `-i` implemented, t/run/switches.t reached its own permission probe

  chmod 0500, $tmpinplace;
  my $canwrite = open my $fh, ">", $check;     # perl: 0, $! = EACCES

and PCL aborted the form with `Error opening #P".../check": Permission denied`.

perl's `open` returns FALSE for every OS refusal and puts the errno in `$!`.
CL's `open` SIGNALS a FILE-ERROR for all of them; the only one PCL answered was
ENOENT, and only because the `<` arm asks for it with `:if-does-not-exist NIL`.

PROBED 5.40.3, nine failing shapes -- SEVEN of them aborted:
  >   into a mode-0500 directory      0, Permission denied
  <   a mode-000 file                 0, Permission denied
  >   onto a DIRECTORY                0, Is a directory
  <   a DIRECTORY                     1 (perl SUCCEEDS; PCL agrees)
  >>  into a mode-0500 directory      0, Permission denied
  +>  into a mode-0500 directory      0, Permission denied
  +>> into a mode-0500 directory      0, Permission denied
  +<  a mode-000 file                 0, Permission denied
  >   through a NON-DIRECTORY path    0, Not a directory

FIX: ONE helper `%p-open-file` (CL `open` + a handler-case that saves errno and
answers NIL), at the six plain-file arms of `%p-open-impl`.  ONLY FILE-ERROR is
caught, deliberately: an OS refusal is perl's answer, and anything else escaping
CL `open` is a PCL bug that must stay loud (rule 12).

SECOND HALF, found by the same round's `+>>` work: an APPEND ANONYMOUS
TEMPORARY needs O_APPEND.  `%p-open-anon-temp` mkstemp'd and set no flag, so
`open($fh,">>",undef); print; seek(0,0); print` OVERWROTE where perl appends --
and that was already wrong for plain ">>" before "+>>" existed.  mkstemp cannot
be asked for the flag, so it is set afterwards with F_SETFL.  Probed over the
four modes: ">>" and "+>>" read back "abcxyz", ">" and "+>" read back "xyz".
That is t/io/perlio_open.t's `check the second write appended` row, which became
visible the moment `open my $fh,'+>>',undef` started working -- the s438
pattern (a fix that makes values real exposes what was passing on nothing),
here fixed in the same commit rather than filed.

RESULT: t/run/switches.t's second abort is gone (shortfall 35 -> 11);
t/io/perlio_open.t 9/1 DIFF -> 10/0 OK.  Guard Pl/t/open-modes-01.t rows 3+6.
subject: perl's `open` never signals -- every OS refusal is FALSE with $! -- but SBCL's `open` signals a FILE-ERROR for all but ENOENT, so seven of nine failing shapes aborted the whole top-level form
